newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Petronas crude oil, gas liquids output up in FY96.
newsitem.headline: Petronas crude oil, gas liquids output up in FY96.

text.p: Malaysia's state-owned oil company, Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas), said on Thursday its crude oil and natural gas liquids output rose by 6.1 percent to 715,000 barrels per day (BPD) in the year ended March 31, 1996.
Production of natural gas increased by 27 percent to 3,759 million standard cubic feet per day (MMSCFD), the company said in a statement to announce its financial results.

Petronas said Malaysia's reserves were estimated at four billion barrels of oil and 80.2 trillion standard cubic feet of gas as at January 1, 1996, making the country's oil and gas reserves the 24th and 11th largest in the world, respectively.
It said 5.77 billion ringgit ($2.31 billion) was invested in domestic exploration and production activities, including those carried out by its exploration arm, Petronas Carigali.
In fiscal 1995/96, an average of 862 MMSCFD of gas was sold to end-users, up 22 percent from 707 MMSCFD the previous year.

"The power sector continued to be the major end-user, accounting for 74 percent of the gas sold with the balance of 18 percent exported to Singapore and eight percent consumed by the industrial, commercial and petrochemical sectors," it said.

The national oil firm announced its net profit for the period under review rose by 48.3 percent to 6.76 billion ringgit. Revenue exceeded 22.25 billion ringgit against 18.1 billion in the previous year.
